note: Graph coherence S_graph (PDF S6): the fraction of edges whose endpoints the trained GNN maps to cosine similarity above tau. Swept over tau, because post-ReLU embeddings are non-negative and any single low threshold marks every edge coherent.

controls.rewired: same edge count between the same nodes, drawn at random

reading: Real edges are markedly more coherent than rewired ones -- at tau = 0.980, 0.718 against 0.367 (+0.351). The graph's wiring is not arbitrary. But an untrained encoder of the same shape scores 0.843 on those same edges -- higher than the trained one -- so this coherence is a property of how the graph was built (edges are thresholded on feature cosine similarity) rather than something training produced. Training slightly *reduces* it, which is what an encoder learning to tell adjacent segments apart would do.
